clue.text: Obstructs Us train by tying her (distressingly) to tracks?

parts.note: dams obstructs a flow, as a dam blocks a river
the El is the American name for an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A villain halts an American train by lashing a woman to the rails, silent-film style.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stock melodrama heroine, the maiden in distress tied to the railway line; 'by tying' just links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The helpless maiden of melodrama is the classic victim strapped to the rails before the locomotive arrives.

clue.text: … is panicking identical soldier in worse luck!

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the exclamation of regret

parts.note: alas is the sigh meaning worse luck
the same soldier as in the clue before, the Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone continues the previous thought, panicking because a twin soldier turns up at a bad moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from MERMAN, whose 'soldier at sea' was RM; 'identical' asks for that same soldier again.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarms are bouts of sudden fear, so a state of panic can be called alarms.

clue.text: Specific gravity about perfect denial, broadcast without pomp

indicators.note: about means the two-letter abbreviation goes round the outside of the rest

parts.note: SG is the standard scientific abbreviation for specific gravity

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A scientist modestly refuses to boast about a perfect measurement on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humble who plays down their own merits speaks without pomp or swagger.

clue.text: Bananas containing potassium and energy rush

indicators.note: containing means the crazy word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, as is loopy
K is the chemical symbol for potassium
snap is vim or energy, as in 'put some snap into it'

explanation.surface: Bananas, rich in potassium, give an energy boost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a health claim about bananas; here bananas is the word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To look snappy is an imperative idiom meaning hurry up, so it is a call to rush.

clue.text: Entertainer rectified a need, always beset by injury, …

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the harm word goes round the outside

parts.note: injury and damage are both harm

indicators.note: rectified means set right, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: ever is an old word meaning always

explanation.surface: A performer repairs a shortfall while dogged by a constant injury.
explanation.walkthrough: DAME EDNA EVERAGE was the comic Australian housewife character played by Barry Humphries. 'rectified' rearranges A NEED into EEDNA, then EVER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a stage and television comic persona, so she is an entertainer.

clue.text: … pleased she often has this to flourish

definitions.text: she often has this to flourish
definitions.meaning: the 'she' is the entertainer of the previous clue, who brandished gladioli on stage; the flowers are known for short by a four-letter clip

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the entertainer is delighted with the prop she waves about.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to DAME EDNA EVERAGE, whose trademark was throwing gladioli to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad means happy, and glads is a florist's clipping of gladioli, the star's flourished flowers.

clue.text: Complicated formula: it involves lands where 25 trains?

indicators.note: involves means the shuffled letters enclose the landing word
complicated means tangled up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: lights, as in alights, means lands or comes to rest

explanation.surface: A tricky equation describes the places where a pilot practises landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is AVIATRIX, a woman pilot; she would train in a cockpit simulator. 'Complicated' rearranges FORMULA IT into FIMULATOR, which goes round LIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit replica on the ground lets a trainee pilot practise without leaving the hangar.

clue.text: Tract inspiring poets left pack leader vacantly nonplussed

parts.note: Akela is the leader of a Cub Scout pack, named after the wolf in Kipling's Jungle Book

indicators.note: vacantly means emptied of its contents, keeping only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A wilderness inspired the poets, but the pack leader was left baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District in north-west England inspired the 'Lake Poets' Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District region of Cumbria gave its name to Wordsworth and his circle, the Lake Poets.

clue.text: Go-ahead, limited liability company initially acquired by a jet manufacturer

indicators.note: acquired by means taken into, so the initials go inside the other pieces

parts.note: Lear is the maker of the Learjet business jet

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of those three words

explanation.surface: A small firm gets bought by an aircraft maker after regulatory approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission to proceed is a go-ahead, the signal that danger is past.

clue.text: Sweep around everyone in dancing venue

indicators.note: around means the sweeping word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a broom is used to sweep
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps up around everybody in a dance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hall for formal dancing is where the waltz and foxtrot are held.

clue.text: Salacious look into Director-General's kink

indicators.note: into means the leering look is put inside the abbreviation

parts.note: DG is the abbreviation for Director-General, as of the BBC
to ogle is to look lecherously

explanation.surface: A lecherous glance reveals something odd about the head of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a sharp bend, as on a golf hole, so it is a kink in a line.

clue.text: Couturier departs in lightly watered crepe at last

indicators.note: in places the departure abbreviation inside the damp word

parts.note: something lightly watered is moist, slightly wet
D stands for departs in timetables

indicators.note: at last means take only the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: A fashion designer walks away from a damp crepe dress at the end of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a milliner or dressmaker, a maker of fashionable clothes like a couturier.

clue.text: African republic's millions after start of last month's support for the dollar, say

indicators.note: after means the republic and millions follow the date piece

parts.note: the start of the year's last month is 1 December, written DEC 1, with the 1 read as I
Mali is a republic in West Africa

explanation.surface: An African country's millions shored up the American currency from the start of December.
explanation.walkthrough: The dollar is divided into 100 cents, a decimal system; DEC 1 reads as DECI.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimalism is the advocacy of decimal systems, the basis of the hundred-cent dollar.

clue.text: Perchance wilt, after winter, as happened to thee?

indicators.note: putting thee in the place of see swaps the opening S sound for TH, as a lisper would

parts.note: happened to see gives saw, the past tense of see

explanation.surface: Something perhaps wilted after a hard winter, just as happened to you, archaically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happened to see' is SAW; the clue says 'happened to thee', so the S becomes TH. 'Perchance wilt' is archaic for 'perhaps will', which is what ice does after winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow and ice may well melt once the cold season ends, so a spring melt is what perhaps will follow.

clue.text: Candour in flyers about fashionable society

indicators.note: about means the aircraft word goes round the trendy word

parts.note: planes are flyers
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Frankness among pilots about high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainness of speech is frankness and openness.

clue.text: I'm sure to be zonked

indicators.note: zonked means knocked about or stoned, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A drug taker admits they are bound to end up stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue is what a drug taker might say: certain to be zonked, or stoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug taker, said of narcotics, is one certain to get high.

clue.text: Location for Prom transmitted around High Barnet (and wide)

indicators.note: around means the sending word wraps the hairstyle

parts.note: sent means transmitted
barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair); an afro hairstyle is tall and broad

explanation.surface: A broadcast from High Barnet, a London suburb, at a seaside promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: High Barnet is a north London district; 'Prom' is a seaside promenade, not a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside promenade runs along the waterfront of a resort town.

clue.text: On this kind of race, wife is blowing a lot

indicators.note: on this means the wife letter sits in front of the answer, so taking it away from the breezy word leaves what is wanted

parts.note: windy weather has a lot of wind blowing

explanation.surface: Because of this race, the wife is huffing and puffing.
explanation.walkthrough: Indy racing is American open-wheel motor racing, named after the Indianapolis 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy names an American motor-racing series, after the Indianapolis 500.

clue.text: Seen in close-up, hem is model's attempt to avoid offence

indicators.note: seen in means the letters can be spotted running through the following words

explanation.surface: A close-up photo shows how a model uses her hem to stay decent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactful mild expression stands in for a blunt one so as not to offend.

clue.text: Article used in pampering?

indicators.note: used in means the article goes inside the care abbreviation

parts.note: TLC is tender loving care, which is pampering
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something applied during a spa treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the powder used when pampering a baby or at a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is applied as a soothing treat for skin, after a bath or for a baby.

clue.text: Curries include this famous one: wade in sloppily

indicators.note: sloppily means carelessly, so these letters are messed about

explanation.surface: A diner is told that curries include a famous ingredient and to tuck in messily.
explanation.walkthrough: Edwina Currie is a British former Conservative minister; Curries here are people with that surname, not Indian dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Of everyone surnamed Currie, the best known is the politician, a former health minister.

clue.text: Wide character was poorly transmitted

parts.note: an em is a printing measure, the width of a capital M
ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A broad-minded person was badly broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide character' is the typographer's em, the wide letter space.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending a message electronically is transmitting it.

clue.text: Daily grind beset by means of movement for many who brought down dictator

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the transport word goes round the routine word

parts.note: a bus carries many passengers
a rut is a dull daily routine

explanation.surface: The tedium of the commute weighs on the many who toppled a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Brutus was one of the assassins of Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the conspiracy that stabbed Julius Caesar to death in 44 BC.

clue.text: Serve up big cheeses for wide boy

indicators.note: serve up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: VIPs are very important people, big cheeses

explanation.surface: A dodgy trader serves important guests.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a flashy small-time crook or black-marketeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms are British slang for a smartly dressed petty swindler.

clue.text: Pilot's velocity in flying air taxi

definitions.note: pilot is: the apostrophe s links definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in places the speed symbol inside the shuffled letters
flying here means sent in all directions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: v is the symbol for velocity in physics

explanation.surface: A pilot's speed when flying an air taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviatrix is a woman aviator, a female pilot.

clue.text: Limitless finance (with origin obscured) keeps northern European

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the shortened word encloses the compass abbreviation
the origin of a word is its first letter; obscuring it drops that letter

parts.note: funding means finance
NE is northeast, the northern European direction

explanation.surface: Endless money, of hidden source, maintains a Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with origin obscured' removes the F from FUNDING, leaving UNDING, which keeps NE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unending goes on without limit or end.

clue.text: Soldier at sea when trapped by skilful one at home there …

indicators.note: when trapped by means the soldier sits inside the other word

parts.note: mean is slang for skilful, as in 'plays a mean guitar'
a Royal Marine, RM, is a soldier who serves at sea

explanation.surface: A marine at sea is caught by an expert who lives there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' refers back to 'at sea': a mythical sea-dweller is at home in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The male counterpart of a mermaid lives in the ocean.
